_comment: re/findings/can.md section 3 HYPOTHESIS: TouCAN modules B (0x707400) and
C (0x707800) are wired to the SAME physical Antrieb-CAN.  It matters
because all four spare receive slots are on module C (can.md section 6):
if C is on a wire we cannot reach, the flex-fuel frame from the Pico node
has nowhere to go.
The check is one short log with ONLY the powertrain pair connected (no
gateway-bridged traffic, engine running or at least KL15 on with the
other bus modules present):
python3 logging/med9log.py log --session logging/sessions/can_bc_check.json \
--bus gs_usb:0 --seconds 20 -o logs/2026-xx-xx_can_bc.csv
Reading the result:
* all three state words live (bit1 toggling / bit0 set, and the data
bytes changing) => B and C share the wire.  HYPOTHESIS confirmed, the
spare slots on C are usable.
* the module-B word (0x802B08, id 0x1A0 Bremse_1) alive but both
module-C words dead => C is a second, separate bus and can.md section 6
has to be redone.
* nothing alive => the wiring or the log is wrong, not the hypothesis.
state-word bits (can.md section 4): bit0 object enabled, bit1 new data
accepted this cycle.  The 8 data bytes of a slot are at 0x803EE8 + 12*slot.

vars.name: can_state_1A0_modB
vars.notes: id 0x1A0 Bremse_1, TouCAN B buffer 0 -- the reference: this one MUST be alive

vars.name: can_data_1A0_modB
vars.notes: split_bytes writes eight rows can_data_1A0_modB_0..7; bytes that change prove traffic
